children: Wall Street rebounded Thursday as easing oil prices helped relieve inflation concerns and supported a recovery in equities following Wednesday’s selloff.
Seeking Alpha analyst Leo Nelissen of
said the session underscored the importance of energy markets in shaping conditions and sentiment.

“Today’s market action shows what goes on in the market,” Nelissen stated, arguing that Wednesday’s decline reflected concerns that Federal Reserve tightening against supply-driven inflation could squeeze the economy.
Nelissen said oil’s weakness has provided relief by reducing inflation fears and allowing Treasury yields to decline.
“Today’s market action happened after two weak days for oil,” he said, adding that the move “eases inflation fears and allows bond rates to fall.”
He identified the Iran conflict and its effect on energy prices as the theme influencing markets as investors assess the Federal Reserve’s policy path.
“It’s one of the reasons why it’s all about the Iran War and its impact on oil,” Nelissen said. “The biggest theme driving returns right now.”
The comments highlight how shifts in energy prices can influence inflation expectations, bond yields, and overall equity performance.

title: SA analyst: Falling oil prices ease key inflation fears
